champion: Chronic osteomyelitis of the temporal bone

facts.raw_span: unilateral otomandibular syndrome (OMS) associated with severe temporal bone hypoplasia
history of deep unilateral neck cellulitis
discharge through the artificial ear canal during the second episode of cellulitis
collection in the right parapharyngeal space and neck collection
hypodense lesion was noted in the middle ear
fistula originating from the middle ear
hyperintense 23-mm lesion at the edge of the petrous bone
2-centimeter mass found during drilling of the hypoplastic petrous bone
millimetric fistula at the tip of the mastoid running into the sternocleidomastoid muscle
first episode occurred in 2014 with no obvious cause
second episode occurred in 2021
recurrence of neck cellulitis two months after the second episode
